scope_lock.source: Round-4 remediation (fresh independent review r6): C15 durable benchmark-failure ledger reserved under D1/C10-style provenance and bound into C9 freeze digest+generation; an exact, narrow, sequence-bound legacy-bridge boot-window (R0-01/R1-01/R1-02 build-only, no invoke, no partial publish) replacing an implicit bootstrap exemption; C13 review_epoch scoping repair_round's attempt_index to the current PASS-closed epoch, plus an authorized_evolution PASS-freshness binding fix; C14 treeDigest removed as redundant with an attested baseCommit; preserves public 8, dual-run, ownership, legacy bridge, 9 tasks, ready=false. Follow-up hardening within the same round: advanceBaseline/resolveFailure crash-ordering fixed exact — idempotent-resume, validate-before-mutate, no faked cross-file atomicity (I11). Round-5 remediation (fresh independent review R7, verdict FAIL: 2 Critical/1 High/1 Medium/1 Low): C15 resolve-bypass closed via C9 remediatedFailureIds (gate-proven copy, exact-equal C12 resolvedFailureIds, I12); C1 authorized_evolution durable-spec check corrected to the real workflow_policy.planning_depth field with authoring.requirements/design validated as a separate lifecycle check; legacy-bridge artifact now captures an exact bootWindowBaseCommit durably, C14.baseCommit verified equal to it (no merge-base guess); C4 planning_depth enum corrected to None|Compact|Full (dropped invalid Standard); V9 reachability moved to the real validate-spec-output.cjs via a new R6-01 read anchor and R1-01 dependency edge; corrected a live C1/C9 digest-binding contradiction (C1 forbids only release-candidate lifecycle digests, not its own spec/review authority digests). Round-8 remediation (live lifecycle detection, no external review round; general-contract fixes only): closed an authoring-lifecycle ordering gap via new I15/R3.7 — a required authoring stage becomes validated only as the direct current-run output of validate-spec-output.cjs plus spec-ground.cjs over its own exact bytes, strictly before the reviewer computes any digest claiming to cover it, and any later edit reverts that stage to draft until re-confirmed; closed an L0 bridge integrity gap via new I16 — the lifecycle worker preflights every finalizer-required condition on an unpersisted candidate before writing the staged bridge artifact, which remains unconsumed until the finalizer's own atomic ready_for_implementation=true promotion (the literal SPEC_READY event), with rollback/quarantine of the exact artifact and temp evidence (never in-place edit, never cross-digest reuse) on any finalizer failure short of that promotion; stated new I17 fixing this checkout's own canonical packages/spec/src/claude/scripts//packages/spec/scripts source authority for every L0-gate/verification command, forbidding a self-installed .claude/.codex projection as an L0 bypass; hardened R3.3/C13/I10 with an explicit reject-before-append check so a review_epoch whose latest entry already shows lifecycle_disposition BLOCKED refuses the whole finalizer operation outright before any attempt_index is computed; added a general, append-only, fail-closed, provenanced C15 reclassifyFailure correction mechanism (new I18, amended R1.9/R5.6) so a misclassified benchmark failure is corrected only by a fresh-adjudicated reclassified event that deriveFailureState folds as the most recent classification, never an in-place rewrite, and never a silent, permanent release-path opener; declared a new I19 single-process concurrent-writer model for every read-modify-write authority/ledger/freeze transition, stating explicitly that write-temp-then-rename gives single-write atomicity and crash-safe resume only, never arbitration between two genuinely concurrent callers; D11's normative sequence, the plan's boot-window narrative, and every affected task's Acceptance/Verification Plan were updated consistently with no case-specific branch; ready remains false and semantic_review remains not-run — this round edits only authoring artifacts, it does not run the finalizer or fabricate a PASS.

criteria.text: When any path under the D1 sole normative protected allowlist is proposed for edit, the change-firewall gate shall require the C1 discriminated union. `benchmark_remediation` alone shall require `primary_failure_class`, `invariant_id`, `hypothesis`, `owner_layer`, `evidence`, `true_positive_family`, `negative_control_family`, `rollback_condition`, and non-empty C15 `failure_ids`; `authorized_evolution` alone shall require `spec_ref`, `spec_semantic_digest`, `independent_pass_receipt_digest`, `planned_write_set`, `negative_control_family`, and `rollback_condition`, and shall forbid every remediation-only field including `primary_failure_class` and `failure_ids`. Unknown or cross-variant fields fail closed. Neither variant shall embed treeDigest, baselineCommit, packageVersion, candidateDigest, baselineAuthorityDigest, or baselineGeneration.

`createFreezeManifest` and `verifyFreezeManifest` shall always load the C15 ledger and bind `failureLedgerDigest` (sha256 of the current ledger bytes, or `NO_FAILURES_ATTESTATION_DIGEST` when the ledger file does not exist) and `failureLedgerGeneration` (the ledger's own `generation`, or `null` when absent) into the freeze, and shall include both fields in `candidateDigest`'s stable binding. Any mismatch between the freeze's bound ledger digest/generation and the ledger's current digest/generation shall exit 2, exactly as an authority digest/generation mismatch does — any accepted C15 ledger event (of any current or future named type) recorded after a freeze was created makes that freeze stale and it must be recreated; this rule is stated generically over "any accepted event," never as an enumerated, recount-prone list of event type names, so a future C15 transition never requires a matching update here.

Publishing a release shall be exactly **three** independent single-file-atomic persistence events, never two, in this fixed order, never reordered or run concurrently, and never described or treated as one cross-file transaction: (A) `advanceBaseline` shall persist the canonical C12 receipt bytes at `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/release-receipt.json`; (B) `advanceBaseline` shall then rotate the C10 authority (`release-baseline.json`) — the sole publication checkpoint; (C) `resolveFailure` shall append a C15 `resolved` event to `benchmark-failure-ledger.json`, once per `resolvedFailureIds` id, invoked separately and strictly after `advanceBaseline` returns success. `advanceBaseline` shall check, before any other read or write, whether the current C10 authority's `releaseReceiptDigest` already equals the supplied receipt's own computed digest. When it does, `advanceBaseline` shall **not** return success on that digest match alone: it shall verify that the canonical persisted receipt exists, conforms to the exact C12 schema, and its own recomputed digest equals the published one, and only then return success without touching the freeze, candidate, or ledger; when the canonical file is missing or fails this verification but the supplied bytes for this call independently verify against the published digest and schema, `advanceBaseline` shall idempotently repair event (A) by re-persisting those exact supplied bytes at the canonical path, re-verify the write, and then return success — recovery of evidence for an already-published fact, never a new publication, requiring no re-validation of freeze/candidate state; when the supplied bytes themselves fail schema or digest verification, `advanceBaseline` shall exit 2 without writing and shall never reconstruct or guess receipt content. Otherwise (a genuinely new candidate), `advanceBaseline` shall perform every read-only validation, then event (A), then — strictly before event (B) ever runs — shall re-read the canonical persisted receipt bytes that write actually produced and verify an exact byte match (or, equivalently, a freshly recomputed digest plus exact C12 schema match) against the supplied receipt, exactly the same read-after-write verification the idempotent-repair branch above already performs on its own write; a mismatch (a physically corrupted write, a concurrent clobber, or a filesystem fault) shall exit 2 without ever running event (B), leaving the C10 authority exactly as it was and never returning `published`; only a verified event (A) shall be followed by event (B), and `advanceBaseline` shall never invoke `resolveFailure` itself. `resolveFailure` shall independently re-load the current C10 authority and refuse (exit 2, no write) unless that authority already shows the exact `release_receipt_digest` it is asked to append as published; it shall be idempotent per `failure_id` (a matching prior `resolved` event is a no-op; a mismatched one is refused, never coerced). A crash before event (A) shall leave nothing written; a crash after event (A) but before event (B) shall leave a staged, valid, unpublished receipt with the C10 authority and ledger unchanged — never described as "nothing written" — recoverable by re-invoking the same sequence; a crash after event (B) shall be recoverable by re-invoking `advanceBaseline` (its hardened idempotency check) followed by the `resolveFailure` loop, with no separate reconciliation command required and no partially-applied file write ever left inconsistent.

`createFreezeManifest` shall set C9's `remediatedFailureIds` by copying the accepted C1 `benchmark_remediation.failure_ids` array exactly, and only after `assertHotspotChangeAllowed` has already proven the open-failure path-union invariant for those exact ids — never independently chosen, supplemented, or caller-supplied at freeze time. For `authorized_evolution` and for `changeKind = no_protected_change`, `remediatedFailureIds` shall always be the empty array. `remediatedFailureIds` shall be included in `candidateDigest`'s stable binding. `advanceBaseline` shall verify that C12's `resolvedFailureIds` is the exact sorted-unique-set equal of the current freeze's `remediatedFailureIds`, exiting 2 on any divergence, so a release receipt can never claim to resolve a failure that was not actually proven-remediated at gate/freeze time. `resolveFailure` shall only ever be invoked, per `resolvedFailureIds`, over ids that trace this exact chain (C1 gate proof → freeze binding → receipt equality → ledger resolution); no separate proposal store shall be introduced — C9 remains the sole durable vehicle carrying this gate-time proof forward to C12.

`resolveFailure` shall never trust a caller-supplied `release_receipt_digest` or a caller's claim that a given `failure_id` belongs to the release being resolved. As event (A) of the three-event publication sequence (R1.11), strictly before event (B) (its authority rename), `advanceBaseline` shall durably persist the exact validated C12 receipt bytes at the canonical path `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/release-receipt.json`, resolved from a fixed trusted project/runtime root; production `advanceBaseline`/`resolveFailure` calls shall accept no per-call caller-supplied alternate path — an isolated trusted root may be bound only when constructing a test/harness instance of the module, with containment verified once at construction time. `resolveFailure` shall independently read those exact bytes, recompute `releaseReceiptDigest` over them, require an exact match against the current C10 authority's own published `releaseReceiptDigest`, validate the bytes conform to the exact C12 key set, and require the `failure_id` it is asked to append to be a member of that receipt's own `resolvedFailureIds` array — refusing (exit 2, no write) on any digest mismatch, schema violation, or absent membership, even when the current published digest is otherwise correct and even when the id names a real, currently open `framework_regression` ledger entry. When the canonical receipt evidence has been lost or corrupted after a prior successful publish, `advanceBaseline`'s own idempotency check (R1.11) shall repair it from cryptographically-proven-correct supplied bytes before `resolveFailure` is ever invoked again — `resolveFailure` itself never repairs, reconstructs, or guesses receipt content.

The legacy-bridge artifact `specs/cafekit-semantic-eval-firewall/reports/bootstrap-legacy-bridge-review.json` is outside the current 10-task DAG and is never owned/written by a feature task. A fresh independent reviewer supplies PASS evidence; the dedicated pre-implementation lifecycle worker preflights structural validation, grounding, C16-fresh authoring, current semantic digest, and zero blockers before its sole atomic write capturing the exact current HEAD as `bootWindowBaseCommit`. Exact keys are schema_version fixed `"1"`, verdict fixed `"PASS"`, blocking_count fixed 0, reviewed_criteria, semantic_digest, bootWindowBaseCommit, written_at. It remains staged until finalizer SPEC_READY; failure before promotion quarantines/deletes it and requires a fresh review/preflight. R0-01 only asserts its exact already-existing bytes and never creates or modifies it.

When `change_intent = benchmark_remediation` and the primary failure class is not `framework_regression`, the gate shall refuse that proposal. This refusal applies only within the `benchmark_remediation` branch; it shall not block a distinct, valid `authorized_evolution` proposal for a legitimate change to the same or another protected path (see R1.7), and the gate shall never treat every product change to a protected path as automatically blocked.

Freeze and release-preflight shall load baseline authority only from tracked `packages/spec/benchmarks/release-baseline.json` and shall reject any CLI, environment, or caller base override with exit code 2. The environment channel is a closed, exactly-enumerated boundary, never an open-ended name-shape guess over `process.env`: the gate shall reject presence (checked by exact key name via `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty`, never by value, and never logged) of exactly these six reserved keys — `CAFEKIT_BASE_COMMIT`, `CAFEKIT_BASELINE_COMMIT`, `CAFEKIT_BASE_REF`, `CAFEKIT_BASELINE_REF`, `CAFEKIT_BASE_PATH`, `CAFEKIT_BASELINE_PATH` — and no other environment variable name, however base/baseline-shaped, is ever inspected, pattern-matched, or treated as an override attempt. An environment key this runtime never reads cannot influence baseline authority and is not an override channel by definition; a name merely shaped like `*BASE*`/`*BASELINE*` (including a third-party ambient var such as `GITHUB_BASE_REF`, or an unrecognized name such as `OVERRIDE_BASE_COMMIT`) is never a supported channel and must never be read as one. `deriveProtectedChangedPaths` shall exclude the reserved `release-baseline.json` path before computing the working-tree diff against authority baselineCommit, then self-derive protected changed paths under the D1 allowlist, excluding `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/**`; reserved-path exclusion takes precedence over the generic `packages/spec/benchmarks/` prefix match. Callers shall not supply empty changedPaths that replaces derivation. Validity of empty derived protected paths depends on authority `state`, not on `baselineCommit == HEAD` alone: when `state = bootstrap`, empty derived protected paths always exit 2 — bootstrap requires a real independent-PASS digest over a non-empty change set; when `state = released`, empty derived protected paths are always valid, including when `baselineCommit == HEAD`, and this is the normal clean-pack path. There is no blanket rule that exits 2 solely on `baselineCommit == HEAD` with empty paths regardless of authority state. baselineCommit shall be a git ancestor of HEAD or equal HEAD. Authority uses C10 discriminated union bootstrap vs released. Named reserved transitions bootstrapBaseline and advanceBaseline are the only writers of release-baseline.json; arbitrary out-of-band edits of that file still fail loadBaselineAuthority/assertBaselineUsable and exit 2, even though the path is excluded from C1 derivation. advanceBaseline runs only after a valid C12 release receipt matching the current freeze and candidate, atomically rotates authority, and invalidates freeze so no valid freeze remains until a new freeze. Freeze shall bind baselineAuthorityDigest and baselineGeneration so authority change invalidates prior freeze. `previousBaselineDigest` in a released-state record shall be sourced from the authority record's own bytes as `loadBaselineAuthority` actually returned immediately before the write — never caller-supplied or self-declared in the same write. `loadBaselineAuthority` shall apply exact load rules for: an absent first record (only bootstrapBaseline may create it; every other command exits 2); an uncommitted named bootstrap/advance write (trusted as current authority without requiring a prior git commit); a committed tracked record (read normally); and an out-of-band edit (detected via a generation/digest chain that cannot be reproduced from any valid transition input, exit 2 on next use). This provenance check is honest-agent tamper detection (accidental edits, buggy scripts, third parties without commit access) — it does not defend against a hostile actor already holding legitimate commit/push authority on the same account.

Mutable freeze state shall live only at `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/change-firewall-freeze.json`, outside D1 allowlist, tree-digest inputs, and npm package files; callers shall not override that path. R0 shall own gitignore of `.cafekit-release/`. Freeze shall compute digests then write. Verification shall exclude freeze state from derivation. Release-preflight and prepack/prepublishOnly shall always require a valid freeze matching current authority generation and digest, and exit 2 when missing, malformed, or stale after advance, including when protected paths are empty. Empty protected paths are valid only when authority state is released, and in that case require changeKind `no_protected_change` and NO_CHANGE_ATTESTATION_DIGEST; empty protected paths during bootstrap state are never valid (see R1.3). Non-empty paths require a C1 proposal covering exact derived paths; C9 alone holds digest bindings.

computeProtectedTreeDigest shall hash sorted paths with type, mode, and content or delete sentinel. proposalDigest shall hash C1 proposal bytes or equal NO_CHANGE_ATTESTATION_DIGEST. candidateDigest shall bind exactly the field set design contract C9 defines — **C9 is the sole canonical, exact field-list authority for this binding; this criterion mirrors it and must never drift from it** — currently baselineAuthorityDigest, baselineGeneration, baselineCommit, failureLedgerDigest, failureLedgerGeneration, remediatedFailureIds, changedPaths, treeDigest, proposalDigest, and packageVersion, without including candidateDigest in its own input. Freeze creates; release/prepack only verify and never self-heal.

Real callers shall be freeze create, release-preflight, prepack, and prepublishOnly. R0 shall surgically wire package.json scripts while preserving the existing version field value. R0 shall own semantic-firewall test discovery in run-skill-self-tests with `--require-semantic-test`; aggregate test runs all discovered `*.semantic-firewall.test.js`. R0 verification requires only R0 basenames and a deliberately failing sentinel nonzero when injected.

When a ChangeProposal declares `change_intent = authorized_evolution` for a legitimate feature, compatibility, security, or maintenance change to a D1 protected path, the gate shall accept it only when: the spec at the declared `spec_ref` has its own `workflow_policy.planning_depth` — the real durable-spec field — equal to `Compact` or `Full` (never `None`); separately, as its own distinct lifecycle-state check and never as a stand-in for `planning_depth`, that spec's `authoring.requirements` and `authoring.design` both equal `validated` **and** are fresh per C16 — that spec's `validation.authoring_validation` receipt is present and its stored `requirements`/`design` digests exactly equal digests freshly recomputed over `spec_ref`'s current `requirements.md`/`design.md` bytes (a `validated` reading with no matching fresh receipt digest is treated identically to `draft` and fails this check, I20); `spec_semantic_digest` equals that spec's current semantic_model digest (fresh, not stale); `independent_pass_receipt_digest` equals the **latest accepted PASS** in that spec's `semantic_review_history` lineage (I14) — the entry with `verdict = PASS` and the numerically highest `sequence` among all entries whose own stored `semantic_digest` field also equals that same current digest — never a lower-sequence match when a higher-sequence matching entry exists in the same lineage (a superseded citation), never an entry from a different spec or `lineage_id`, and never a digest-mismatched entry regardless of its own sequence; `planned_write_set` is the exact sorted-set match of the derived protected changedPaths; and `rollback_condition` plus `negative_control_family` are present. This rebinding rule means a legitimate post-PASS requirements/design correction never self-locks `authorized_evolution`: the superseded entry simply stops matching, and a fresh re-PASS at a higher `sequence` in the same lineage immediately becomes the new latest accepted PASS every subsequent proposal cites. The gate shall refuse `authorized_evolution` unconditionally, with no citation or field able to pass it through, whenever the derived paths resolve to a currently open (unclassified or classified `framework_regression`, unresolved) C15 ledger entry; `authorized_evolution` carries no `failure_ids` field and is never accepted merely because a proposal cites one — such a change shall use `benchmark_remediation` instead, citing the exact `failure_ids`. Rejecting a non-`framework_regression` class inside `benchmark_remediation` (R1.2) shall not be read as a blanket refusal of every legitimate product change to a protected path.

`bootstrapBaseline` shall accept only a C14 `BootstrapAttestation` with an exact `baseCommit` that equals the `bootWindowBaseCommit` field durably captured in the legacy-bridge artifact (`specs/cafekit-semantic-eval-firewall/reports/bootstrap-legacy-bridge-review.json`, see D11) at the moment of the legacy-bridge ceremony — a fact recorded once, before any boot-window code landed, never later reconstructed from git history or a merge-base guess — and that is also a real git commit object and an ancestor of or equal to an exact `headCommit` that equals the actual current HEAD at run time, plus a `bootstrapReviewDigest` bound to the seed `semantic_review_history` entry's `review_receipt_digest` (the fresh, real, post-C2/C13-cutover PASS at sequence 0/review_epoch 0 — see R1.9/D11/I9; never the disposable legacy 2-key bridge report). C14 has no `treeDigest` field; `bootstrapBaseline` independently re-derives the protected tree digest at `baseCommit` itself rather than trusting a caller-attested copy, since `baseCommit` already pins the tree. Protected paths for the bootstrap change-set shall be self-derived from the `baseCommit`..`headCommit` diff under D1 (spanning the exact full boot-window diff); the caller shall not supply `changedPaths` directly. `bootstrapBaseline` shall refuse to run before the seed `semantic_review_history` entry exists, and shall write generation 0 with `baselineCommit = baseCommit` explicitly. There shall be no implicit `origin/main`, empty-tree base, or merge-base guess, and no caller base override outside this one-time attested bootstrap; every subsequent routine freeze shall read only the authority record.

The change-firewall shall own a durable C15 `BenchmarkFailureLedger` at `packages/spec/benchmarks/benchmark-failure-ledger.json` with an adjacent exact schema, exporting `loadFailureLedger`, `assertFailureLedgerUsable`, `openFailure`, `classifyFailure`, `reclassifyFailure`, `resolveFailure`, `computeFailureLedgerDigest`, `deriveFailureState`, and `NO_FAILURES_ATTESTATION_DIGEST`; this file shall be a reserved control-plane path excluded from generic C1 diff derivation before the `packages/spec/benchmarks/` prefix match, exactly like `release-baseline.json`, and R0-01 shall be its sole file-write anchor. `openFailure` shall append an `opened` event with a unique `failure_id`, sorted exact `paths`, `candidate_digest`, `evidence_digest`, and `occurred_at`; `classifyFailure` shall append a `classified` event with `primary_failure_class` and a fresh C5 `adjudication_digest` only for a `failure_id` with an `opened` event and no prior `classified` event; `reclassifyFailure` shall append a `reclassified` event only for a `failure_id` with a prior `classified` (or `reclassified`) event and no prior `resolved` event, requiring an exact `previous_primary_failure_class` match against that `failure_id`'s currently-derived class and a fresh, non-reused C5 `adjudication_digest`, refusing (exit 2, no write) a stale/mismatched `previous_primary_failure_class`, a reused `adjudication_digest`, or any `failure_id` already `resolved`; `resolveFailure` shall append a `resolved` event with `decision_digest` and `release_receipt_digest` only for a `failure_id` classified `framework_regression` with no prior `resolved` event. `deriveFailureState` shall fold events, using the most recent classification-type event (`classified` or `reclassified`) to determine current class, so an entry is blocking while `opened`-only or classified `framework_regression` and unresolved, and nonblocking once classified as any other class or once resolved — a correction back to `framework_regression` immediately re-blocks the entry, and a correction away from it still requires the same fresh-adjudication proof, so no classification change can silently open or permanently close a release path. `assertHotspotChangeAllowed` shall refuse `authorized_evolution` unconditionally when derived paths intersect a blocking ledger entry, and shall accept `benchmark_remediation` only when its `failure_ids` exactly names every intersecting blocking entry and their combined `opened.paths` union equals the proposal's `paths` exactly. `loadFailureLedger`/`assertFailureLedgerUsable` shall fail closed (exit 2) on a missing-when-required, malformed, or provenance-broken ledger for every caller and every `change_intent`, with no bypass; a ledger that has never had `openFailure` called is the legitimate zero-failures state, not malformed.

When authoring-kernel modules define primitives, they shall admit only domain-neutral vocabulary (scope, outcome, decision, assumption, boundary, owner, contract/invariant, acceptance, verification relation, negative relation, unresolved user choice, artifact trigger) and shall not embed product-domain answers as required behavior.
When a domain lens pack is activated, it shall encode only questions and failure relations and shall reject packs that ship expected product values as oracle answers.

When kernel or structural-validator sources are scanned, the ban shall fail closed only on these machine-checkable patterns: (1) literal `prompt_sha256:sha256:` followed by 64 hex digits used as an oracle, (2) a JSON or object map keyed by a public-regression `task_id` from a generic seeded fixture whose values are treated as expected answers, (3) an identifier or key named `expected_domain_answer` bound to a literal. The ban shall not fail solely because prose mentions APIs, retention, or other domain words outside those patterns. Ban tests shall use generic seeded fixtures and shall not require the public-pool task. Legitimate domain constants in authored requirements or design remain allowed.

`validate-spec-output.cjs` shall import and invoke the domain-neutral lens/schema/provenance ban validator unconditionally for Compact and Full semantic models. Missing ban module, invalid lens keys, expected-answer field, benchmark identity field used as oracle, prompt-hash oracle pattern, or skipped invocation shall fail validation. Optional or best-effort wiring language is forbidden.

Owned verification shall include an integration or mutation test that temporarily replaces or instruments the ban validator and proves the real validate entrypoint calls it; a standalone unit test of the ban module alone shall not satisfy this criterion.

When a semantic review completes, `validation.semantic_review` shall use exactly the frozen C2 key set and types: status, semantic_digest, verdict, lifecycle_disposition, findings, unresolved_decisions, graph_coverage, repair_round, reviewed_criteria, counterexamples, and reviewer_evidence. Reviewer verdict is PASS or FAIL; lifecycle_disposition is CONTINUE or BLOCKED; these fields shall not be conflated.

When structural validation and grounding succeed and the receipt verdict is explicit PASS with lifecycle_disposition CONTINUE, zero unresolved blocking findings or decisions, and derived repair_round in 0..2, the readiness finalizer shall be the only writer that may set `ready_for_implementation=true`.

The finalizer shall derive `review_epoch` as the count of prior entries in the same `semantic_review_history` lineage whose `verdict` is PASS (epoch 0 before any PASS; a PASS entry is stamped with the epoch it closes; the next entry opens `review_epoch + 1` at `attempt_index 0`). repair_round shall be the C13 `attempt_index`: the count of prior entries in the **same `review_epoch`** whose `verdict` is FAIL — not the whole lineage's FAIL count. Index values 0, 1, 2 name the first, second, and third attempt of that epoch respectively. PASS at index 0, 1, or 2 may promote when all other gates pass, closing the epoch. FAIL at index 0 or 1 shall leave ready false and permit the next index of the same epoch. FAIL at index 2 (the third attempt of the epoch) shall set lifecycle_disposition BLOCKED, leave ready false, and block any fourth attempt of that epoch from ever occurring (index 3 never occurs within it, and a BLOCKED epoch is never reopened). Before deriving `review_epoch`/`attempt_index` for any new entry or appending it, the finalizer shall first check whether the latest entry already recorded for the current `review_epoch` in this lineage carries `lifecycle_disposition BLOCKED`; when it does, the finalizer shall refuse the entire operation outright — no `attempt_index` computed, no entry appended, no readiness decision changed — rather than silently deriving an out-of-range fourth-attempt index. The finalizer shall atomically append the current completed receipt to `semantic_review_history` together with the readiness decision; a receipt whose `review_receipt_digest` equals any existing entry's digest anywhere in the same lineage — not only the latest entry — is a replay, shall not be appended twice, and shall not increment `attempt_index` or `review_epoch`. Any caller-supplied `repair_round`, `review_epoch`, `semantic_review_history`, or `lineage_id` that diverges from the finalizer-derived state shall be rejected outright — this is the single rule, never a silent ignore. `lineage_id` shall remain stable across ordinary semantic authoring edits per I6; only spec recreation starts a new lineage. Missing or mistyped required fields, stale digest, or blocking unresolved items leave ready false and shall not invent PASS from counterexample shape alone.

When the structural validator inspects a review receipt, it shall enforce C2 key set, types, nullability, enums, cardinality, stable ordering rules for digest inputs, and digest freshness only, and shall not judge semantic meaning.

Automated tests owned by the finalizer task shall prove refuse paths for non-passing incomplete receipts and promote only for explicit PASS with CONTINUE and zero blockers, including at least one negative-control fixture, attempt-index derivation, and index-2 BLOCKED stop with ready false.

When a semantic review completes, `validation.semantic_review_history` shall use exactly the C13 key set: `lineage_id` derived as sha256 of a stable-JSON object over the immutable fields `feature_name` and `created_at`, and `entries` as an append-only array whose items use exactly `sequence`, `semantic_digest`, `review_receipt_digest`, `verdict`, `lifecycle_disposition`, `blocking_count`, `attempt_index`, `review_epoch`. `review_receipt_digest` shall be the sole reference to the full receipt; findings, unresolved_decisions, and counterexamples shall not be duplicated into history. A receipt whose `review_receipt_digest` already matches any existing entry anywhere in the same lineage — not only the latest entry — is a replay and shall not be appended twice.

A required authoring stage (`authoring.requirements`, `authoring.design`, and, when present, `authoring.research`/`authoring.tasks`) shall transition from `draft` to `validated` only as the direct, current-run output of `validate-spec-output.cjs` and `spec-ground.cjs` both completing cleanly over that stage's exact current bytes — never a manual flip, never inferred from a prior run, and never set by the semantic reviewer or the finalizer. The semantic reviewer shall compute `semantic_digest` (and every `graph_coverage`/counterexample claim it produces) only over bytes for which every required stage already shows `validated`; a receipt computed over stage bytes that are later marked `validated` without recomputing the digest is stale and shall not be treated as covering the validated state. Any edit to a stage's authored bytes after it was marked `validated` shall immediately revert that stage to `draft` until validator and grounder both re-confirm it over the new bytes; a `validated` flag left stale against since-changed bytes shall be treated identically to `draft` by every downstream consumer, including `authorized_evolution`'s C1 check (R1.7) and the finalizer's C13 lineage.

`validation.authoring_validation` (C16 `AuthoringValidationReceipt`) shall be `null` until the first successful coordinator run and, once present, shall have exact keys `schema_version` fixed `"1"`, and `requirements`, `design`, `research`, `tasks` — each an object with exact keys `digest` and `validated_at` (ISO string). `digest` for `requirements`/`design` shall be a raw-byte sha256 (colon plus 64 lowercase hex) of that stage's exact current file bytes with no normalization. `digest` for `research` shall be the same raw-byte sha256 of `research.md` when `authoring.research != absent`, or the exact literal sentinel `RESEARCH_ABSENT_DIGEST` when absent. `digest` for `tasks` shall be a sha256 over the stable-JSON canonical bytes of an array of objects, each with exact keys `path` and `digest` — one object per task file, `path` the exact repo-relative path and `digest` the raw-byte sha256 of that task file — sorted by `path` using the same exact ASCII ordinal string comparator C11 defines (never `localeCompare`), or the exact literal sentinel `TASKS_ABSENT_DIGEST` when zero task files exist. None of these digests shall be computed from `semantic_digest`, `review_receipt_digest`, or the receipt's own bytes — no circular digest is possible. A stage is fresh if and only if `authoring.<field> = validated` and the receipt is present and its stored digest for that field exactly equals a digest freshly recomputed, at read time, over that field's exact current bytes by this same algorithm; every other case (`authoring.<field> = validated` with the receipt absent, with no entry for that field, or with a digest mismatch) shall be read as `draft` by every downstream consumer — `validate-spec-output.cjs`, the finalizer, `authorized_evolution`'s C1 check, and `spec-scaffold.cjs` alike (I20).

`packages/spec/src/claude/scripts/spec-authoring-validation.cjs` shall be the sole writer of any `authoring.requirements`/`authoring.design`/`authoring.research`/`authoring.tasks` transition to `validated` and of `validation.authoring_validation`. It shall construct an in-memory candidate spec.json (never persisted until success), invoke the canonical `validate-spec-output.cjs` and `spec-ground.cjs` against that exact candidate's current bytes, compute the R3.8 digests, and only on every check completing cleanly shall it atomically replace spec.json (write-temp-then-rename) with the updated `authoring.*` enum values and the fresh C16 receipt written together in the same replace. Any failure, partial check, or exception shall leave spec.json completely unchanged — no partial persisted state. No other writer — `spec-scaffold.cjs`, the semantic reviewer, the finalizer, or a hand-edit — shall ever set an authoring stage to `validated` or write this receipt (I21); `spec-scaffold.cjs` shall write only `draft` or `absent` for these fields, never `validated`, removing any prior asymmetric preserve-on-migrate behavior for `requirements`/`design`.

When IR mode is `shadow` or `promote`, `spec-semantic-model` projection and the readiness finalizer path shall both invoke the dual-run compare under contract C11, write a disagreement report on mismatch with exact fields defined in C11, persist mode state, support rollback to `shadow` or `off`, and shall not treat an unwired orphan IR module as satisfaction of this criterion.

When mode is `shadow`, markdown projection remains authority for `semantic_model` promotion bytes; disagreements are reported and do not alone flip ready. When mode is `promote` after pre-registered gates, IR becomes authority for the projected semantic model and disagreement hard-fails readiness; otherwise mode stays `shadow` or `off`. Equality and digests shall follow C11 normalize rules only.

IR normalization shall sort every top-level `semantic_model` array (`criteria`, `anchors`, `design_records`, `verification_definitions`) and every nested set array (`subject_criteria`, `proof_criteria`, `decision_refs`, `reachability.anchor_refs`, after de-duplication) using one exact ASCII ordinal string comparator (UTF-16 code-unit comparison, not `localeCompare` or an implementer-chosen "natural sort"). R3-01 shall replace the existing `localeCompare`-based sort call sites in `spec-semantic-model.cjs` with this comparator and shall prove cross-host sort parity with an owned test.

When this repository stores evaluation assets, it shall host only public regression interface, public fixture bodies, and pool contracts; private validation bodies, sealed bodies, oracles, and exposure ledgers remain outside the package tree under bro-owned external storage.

When the pool interface is declared, it shall define three pools sized 8 public, 8 private validation, and 8 sealed; the public pool shall have an in-repo interface file, manifest, and exactly 8 public fixture body files owned by the pool task without private or sealed bodies. Each public fixture body shall conform to C4, including a typed `answer_pattern` made only of domain-neutral predicate/value-shape/lexical-boundary constraints, never an expected answer. The external sealed pool shall rotate for every release candidate, shall never be read by an authoring/tuning run, and a retired sealed case may enter the public pool only after two later releases have completed. D6's exact external-ledger schema and `verify --external-ledger <absolute-file>` contract are mandatory; runtime never scans environment, cwd, or HOME for a ledger, and the fixed untracked pointer digest must match the exact explicit file bytes.

When a candidate run executes, the runner shall create a fresh realpath-resolved isolation root outside the source/package tree, refuse symlink escape or any artifact outside that root, and emit the exact D7 `CandidateRunRecord` bound to `candidateDigest`, run id, failure id when present, corpus generation/digest, and artifact byte digests. An independent C5 adjudicator record shall bind that exact run/candidate/failure tuple plus artifact, corpus, oracle, rubric, reviewer identity, and freshness nonce before any release-ready claim; replay or cross-candidate reuse fails closed.
When package ship inventory is evaluated, B1 harness scripts and private or sealed evaluation payloads shall be excluded from the npm product ship set.
Owned tests shall prove public loaders reject private or sealed body paths and inventory excludes B1 as a product ship surface, with a negative-control attempt that must fail closed.

When a benchmark run surfaces a framework failure, the candidate isolation runner shall invoke C15 `openFailure` with a unique `failure_id`, sorted exact `paths`, `candidate_digest`, and `evidence_digest`; after producing a fresh, non-reused C5 `AdjudicationRecord` for that exact failure/run/candidate, R4-01 shall invoke `classifyFailure` with the canonical C5 record bytes, not a bare caller-asserted digest. C15 shall recompute the digest, verify reviewer identity/freshness and exact failure/run/candidate/evidence bindings, then append it. `reclassifyFailure` shall require a different fresh C5 record bound to the same failure and the exact current `previous_primary_failure_class`. Stale, replayed, cross-run, cross-candidate, post-resolution, or bare-digest classification attempts fail closed.

When a release-affecting decision is formed, C7 shall contain the exact candidate/run/adjudication bindings, one typed result for each of the eight ordered D8 gates, an overall `PASS|FAIL|BLOCKED` decision, and a digest over its canonical bytes. Every gate shall implement C7's closed evidence key set and exact PASS predicate; `release-decision.schema.json` encodes those definitions and may not defer semantics to implementer-authored adjacent fields. A gate passes only with fresh evidence whose candidate/run digests match C7; a missing, unknown, stale, differently-bound, or malformed result is non-PASS. Correctness gates run before cost. The non-inferiority gate passes only when the candidate introduces zero additional hard failures relative to the frozen baseline and its aggregate quality score is greater than or equal to that baseline; equality is allowed, any lower score fails. After a non-PASS at repair_round index 2 with lifecycle disposition BLOCKED, further completed reviews shall not promote, with readiness remaining false.
Claude Code and Codex shall be required release-blocking matrix members; Grok may be optional stress only and shall not alone greenlight release.
When required host evidence is missing, the system shall record a host-blocked or not-ready outcome and shall not simulate host events or downgrade assurance to invent PASS.

Packed Claude Code and Codex source-removed installs shall match on normalized semantic graph and readiness bit for the same reviewed bytes, or record a concrete host blocker; silent divergence fails owned tests.

When `advanceBaseline` runs, it shall require a C12 `ReleaseReceipt` with exact keys `schema_version` fixed `"1"`, `receipt_id`, `status` fixed `"published"`, `baselineAuthorityDigest`, `baselineGeneration`, `freezeDigest`, `candidateDigest`, `treeDigest`, `packageVersion`, `releaseCommit`, `artifactPath`, `artifactDigest`, `resolvedFailureIds`; `releaseReceiptDigest` shall be computed externally over canonical receipt bytes and shall never be a field inside the receipt. `advanceBaseline` shall first check whether the current C10 authority's `releaseReceiptDigest` already equals this receipt's own (per R1.11); when it does, it shall verify — never blindly assume — that the canonical persisted receipt at `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/release-receipt.json` exists, conforms to the exact C12 schema, and its own recomputed digest matches, idempotently repairing that canonical file from the supplied bytes when it is missing or corrupt but the supplied bytes independently verify (R1.11/R1.13); if the digests do not already match, it shall verify the receipt's authority digest/generation, freeze digest, and candidate/tree/package fields against the current freeze and candidate, verify `resolvedFailureIds` is the exact sorted-set equal of the current freeze's `remediatedFailureIds` (R1.12), verify `releaseCommit` exists and is a descendant of or equal to the current baseline, verify `status = "published"`, and independently re-hash the actual bytes at `artifactPath` (restricted to `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/`) to confirm they equal `artifactDigest`, rejecting a symlinked, missing, or content-mismatched artifact; any mismatch exits 2 without writing. On success, `advanceBaseline` shall persist the receipt bytes at the canonical path (event A) before the next released C10 authority stores the externally computed `releaseReceiptDigest` and a `previousBaselineDigest` sourced per C10's exact provenance rule (hashed from the authority record `loadBaselineAuthority` actually returned, never self-declared), `generation + 1`, and `baselineCommit = releaseCommit` (event B), then invalidate the current freeze; these two events are the sole things `advanceBaseline` does and it shall never itself invoke `resolveFailure`.

R5 shall flip IR mode from `shadow` to `promote` only when, on the same candidate: every currently ordered D8 release gate has passed, a fresh independent C5 adjudication record exists for that candidate, Claude/Codex packed parity is confirmed, and the C11 shadow dual-run shows zero disagreements for that candidate. When required host evidence is missing or blocked, mode shall remain `shadow` or `off` and readiness shall remain not-ready. On any promote-mode disagreement, the writer shall immediately roll mode back to `shadow`, the readiness decision for that cycle shall hard-fail, and promote shall not be sticky across the rollback — the next candidate shall re-earn every gate above from `shadow`.

When `advanceBaseline` succeeds (freshly published, idempotently confirmed already-published, or idempotently repaired per R1.11) and the C12 receipt's `resolvedFailureIds` is non-empty, R5-01 shall invoke C15 `resolveFailure` for each id, strictly after `advanceBaseline` has returned, passing only `failure_id` and the current C7 `ReleaseDecision`'s `decision_digest` — never a `release_receipt_digest` R5-01 computed or asserted itself, since `resolveFailure` independently re-derives and verifies the published receipt digest itself (R1.13). `resolveFailure` shall itself independently re-load the current C10 authority and refuse (exit 2, no write) unless that authority already shows this exact `releaseReceiptDigest` as published — so it can never append a `resolved` event for a release `advanceBaseline` has not durably committed — and shall refuse any id that is not classified `framework_regression`, unknown to the ledger, or absent from the persisted receipt's own `resolvedFailureIds`. `resolveFailure` shall be idempotent per id: replaying it for an id already resolved with the same `release_receipt_digest` is a no-op success; replaying it with a different `release_receipt_digest` is refused, never coerced. A crash after event (A) but before event (B) shall leave a staged, unpublished receipt recoverable by retrying `advanceBaseline`; a crash between event (B) and any `resolveFailure` call, or mid-loop across ids, shall be recoverable by re-invoking the same sequence with the same receipt.

The final freeze, C12 `ReleaseReceipt`, and `advanceBaseline` shall not run until every task R0-01 through R6-01 has landed and every D8 release gate has passed on the same candidate; a release receipt whose covered scope is only the boot-window tasks (R0-01, R1-01, R1-02) shall be refused (D11/I9).

C6 shall be a typed registry. Every meaning-preserving transform shall declare an id, input-domain precondition, deterministic transform operation, preserved semantic graph fields, permitted graph delta, and forbidden graph delta; prose literals shall not be the primary oracle.

C6 shall define a minimum critical-mutant catalog covering omitted criterion, weakened boundary/operator, missing failure path, broken dependency/ownership edge, stale provenance binding, and expected-answer leakage. Every framework detector or invariant fix shall name a true-positive family, negative-control family, and the catalog mutants it must kill; generated relations never self-approve.

Owned tests shall prove every applicable critical mutant is killed and every registered meaning-preserving transform satisfies its declared graph contract, with at least one valid negative control that survives and one invalid mutant that is detected.

Migration shall follow inventory, report-only diagnostics, public property coverage, dual-run, promote, and proxy-removal only while mutants still die. Every phase shall emit a machine-readable receipt binding phase id, predecessor receipt digest, candidate digest, success gates, evidence digests, rollback trigger, rollback target, and status; the next phase and release gate shall refuse missing, stale, failed, or out-of-order receipts.

This feature shall declare machine ownership boundaries with disjoint write_sets and dependency-ordered sequential writers, and ownership-contention checking shall be global and pairwise across every boundary in `coordination.boundaries`, not only within one boundary: for any two tasks anywhere in the topology holding a write anchor on the exact same target, that pair shall have a direct DAG edge evidenced by exactly one dependency boundary between them (a producer/consumer pair sharing more than one same-target write conflict is proven by one representative dependency boundary plus the shared registry edge, since the dependency boundary schema carries a single deliverable and a second boundary for the same pair would duplicate the producer in the registry-dependency projection check), or the pairing is a defect regardless of whether the two tasks share one ownership boundary. **The candidate pair set for this scan shall always be derived directly from the complete `anchorsByTask` write-anchor projection — every task's every write anchor, independent of which `coordination.boundaries` entries happen to reference them — never only from declared `write_sets` or from iterating already-declared boundaries; a same-target pair named in no boundary at all is exactly the defect this scan exists to catch, not a case it silently passes.** `validate-spec-output.cjs` is R1-01's sole write anchor within this feature; R1-01 implements this global-scan mechanism as part of its own edit to that file. R6-01 holds a read/consumer anchor on the same file and owns only the negative-fixture proof, never the scan mechanism's own implementation. Owned verification shall include a dual-writer negative fixture with nonzero failing cases covering an in-boundary pair, a cross-boundary pair with no dependency edge, and a synthetic pair whose shared target is named in no `coordination.boundaries` entry at all; every create or modify proof target including R5 proof surfaces shall be listed in the owning task write_set; this is not a new process-wide file lock outside the validator.

The global ownership-contention scan required by R8.2 shall be implemented inside `validate-spec-output.cjs` by R1-01 — the file's sole write-owner within this feature — as part of R1-01's own edit to that file; the scan shall derive every candidate write/write task pair directly from the complete `anchorsByTask` projection, independent of which `coordination.boundaries` entries reference them, and shall treat any single existing dependency boundary between a pair as covering every target that pair shares, regardless of which target it names as its own `deliverable`. R6-01 shall verify this scan via its own owned negative fixture (R8.2) but shall never implement the scan mechanism itself.

After R0-01, R1-01, and R1-02 complete, a lifecycle-only R1-03 task shall require the fresh post-cutover seed PASS at sequence 0/review_epoch 0, validate exact C14 against the captured boot-window base and current HEAD, invoke the already-built bootstrapBaseline once, and atomically persist then byte-re-read `packages/spec/reports/bootstrap-activation.json`. The receipt shall use D15's exact closed key set and R0-owned schema; no caller path override exists. R0-01 owns the dedicated bootstrap activation test, while R1-03 only invokes it; package inventory excludes this source-only execution evidence from npm payload.

R2-01, R3-01, and R4-01 shall depend on R1-03 and shall independently hash the exact activation-receipt bytes, validate its schema, and require its authority digest, commit, and fixed generation 0 to equal the current C10 tail before any protected write; completed predecessor tasks without a matching receipt are insufficient. Missing, stale, differently-bound, nonzero-generation, or replay-conflicting activation fails closed.

design_records.title: ChangeProposal
design_records.text: - **Owner:** R0-01 - **Consumers:** R1-01, R1-02, R2-01, R6-01 - **Shape/behavior:** Tagged union on `change_intent`. Both variants: unknown keys fail closed; neither may contain treeDigest, baselineCommit, packageVersion, candidateDigest, baselineAuthorityDigest, or baselineGeneration; for changeKind no_protected_change, proposal is absent and NO_CHANGE_ATTESTATION_DIGEST is used in C9 only. - **`benchmark_remediation`** — keys exactly: change_intent fixed `"benchmark_remediation"`, proposal_id string, invariant_id string, hypothesis string, owner_layer enum authoring_kernel|structural_compiler|semantic_reviewer|readiness_finalizer|benchmark_controller|independent_adjudicator|release_process, primary_failure_class enum framework_regression|model_runtime_error|prompt_ambiguity|domain_research_failure|infrastructure|oracle_defect|mixed|unknown, paths non-empty array of exact repo-relative file paths, failure_ids non-empty sorted-unique array of C15 `benchmark-failure-ledger.json` `failure_id` strings, evidence non-empty string array, true_positive_family non-empty string array, negative_control_family non-empty string array, rollback_condition string, optional held_out_result string, optional ceremony_delta string. `assertHotspotChangeAllowed` accepts this variant only when derived protected changedPaths and `paths` are sorted-set equal, `primary_failure_class` is exactly `framework_regression`, every id in `failure_ids` resolves (per C15 `deriveFailureState`) to a currently open (`opened`-only or classified `framework_regression` without `resolved`) ledger entry whose `opened.paths` union equals `paths` exactly, and the other required semantic fields are non-empty. A `primary_failure_class` other than `framework_regression` is refused **inside this variant only** — it is not a blanket refusal of every change to a protected path (see `authorized_evolution`). - **`authorized_evolution`** — keys exactly: change_intent fixed `"authorized_evolution"`, proposal_id string, spec_ref string (repo-relative path to a durable Compact or Full spec directory), spec_semantic_digest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex, independent_pass_receipt_digest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex, planned_write_set non-empty sorted-unique array of exact repo-relative paths, rollback_condition string, negative_control_family non-empty string array. `assertHotspotChangeAllowed` accepts this variant only when: the spec at `spec_ref` exists with its own `workflow_policy.planning_depth` — the real durable-spec field — equal to `Compact` or `Full` (never `None`); **separately**, as its own distinct lifecycle-state check and never as a stand-in for `planning_depth`, that spec's `authoring.requirements` and `authoring.design` both equal `validated` (the real `draft|validated|absent` lifecycle enum for those two artifacts — authoring state and planning depth are two independent fields and this gate never conflates them); `spec_semantic_digest` equals that spec's CURRENT `semantic_model` digest (fresh, not stale); `independent_pass_receipt_digest` equals the **latest accepted PASS** in that spec's lineage per I14 — the `semantic_review_history` entry with `verdict = PASS` and the numerically highest `sequence` among all entries **whose own stored `semantic_digest` field also equals that same current `spec_semantic_digest`** — never a lower-sequence match when a higher-sequence matching entry exists in the same lineage (a superseded citation), never an entry from a different spec/lineage, and never a digest-mismatched entry merely cited; `planned_write_set` is the exact sorted-set match of the derived protected changedPaths; and `rollback_condition` plus `negative_control_family` are present. The gate MUST refuse `authorized_evolution` when any of the same derived paths resolves (per C15 `deriveFailureState`) to a currently open (`opened`-only or classified `framework_regression` without `resolved`) ledger entry — such a change must go through `benchmark_remediation` instead, citing that entry's `failure_id`; `authorized_evolution` is never a bypass for an un-adjudicated benchmark failure. For this feature's own boot-window (D11/I9), every R2-01..R6-01 `authorized_evolution` proposal binds `spec_ref` to this same spec and `independent_pass_receipt_digest` to the latest accepted PASS in this spec's own lineage per I14 — ordinarily the seed `sequence 0`/`review_epoch 0` entry itself, and only a later entry in that same lineage if a legitimate post-seed requirements/design correction required a fresh re-PASS (I14 names the exact, unambiguous selection rule and why this never self-locks). - **C16 freshness is part of the canonical C1 branch:** the `validated` enum check above is necessary but never sufficient. `assertHotspotChangeAllowed` must invoke the shared `spec-authoring-digest.cjs` primitive and require the current requirements/design bytes to match C16 exactly; absent/mismatched receipt is draft-equivalent and fails. - **Compatibility:** Additive optional fields forbidden until schema version bump; a third `change_intent` variant requires a schema version bump. `failure_ids` references C15 ledger entries by opaque string label only, never a digest, so C1 and C15 remain non-circular: C15's own `classified`/`resolved` events reference fresh C5/C7/C12 digests, never a C1 proposal digest.

design_records.title: ReleaseBaselineAuthority
design_records.text: - **Owner:** R0-01 - **Consumers:** R5-01, R6-01 - **Shape/behavior:** Tracked JSON `packages/spec/benchmarks/release-baseline.json` is one append-only envelope with exact top-level keys `schema_version` fixed `"2"`, `records`. `records` is a non-empty array ordered by generation; `loadBaselineAuthority` validates the complete array and returns its tail as the current authority, while every consumer-facing authority digest is the digest of that tail record's canonical bytes. Each record is a discriminated union on state: (1) state bootstrap, generation 0, baselineCommit (set from the C14 BootstrapAttestation's exact `baseCommit`, never blank or guessed), baselinePackageVersion, bootstrapReviewDigest sha256 colon plus 64 hex of the seed `semantic_review_history` entry's `review_receipt_digest`, previousBaselineDigest null, transition_witness; it must not include releasedCandidateDigest or releaseReceiptDigest and empty derived protected paths are invalid. (2) state released, generation integer at least 1, baselineCommit equal to release commit, baselinePackageVersion, releaseReceiptDigest sha256 colon plus 64 hex, previousBaselineDigest sha256 colon plus 64 hex of the preceding record's canonical bytes, transition_witness; empty derived protected paths are valid. Named transitions only: `bootstrapBaseline` atomically creates the envelope with exactly the generation-0 record after valid C14 and non-empty protected paths; `advanceBaseline` validates C12/current freeze/candidate, appends exactly one prior-generation-plus-one released record, and atomically replaces the whole envelope, then invalidates freeze. Neither transition rewrites/removes/reorders any prior record. Freeze and preflight are read-only; reserved-path exclusion in D1 applies before diff derivation. Schema `packages/spec/benchmarks/release-baseline.schema.json` describes this exact envelope and closed record union. - **Predecessor provenance (exact, no self-declaration):** `previousBaselineDigest` is never caller-supplied. For every released record, the loader canonicalizes the immediately preceding in-envelope record, recomputes its digest, requires exact equality, requires generation prior plus one, and replays the named transition against the persisted non-secret input binding in `transition_witness`. For generation 0 it requires null predecessor fields and valid C14 input binding. **Load rules:** absent file permits only first `bootstrapBaseline`; both committed and uncommitted envelopes are validated identically from genesis through tail, without trusting git status; any hand edit, deletion/reorder, broken digest, skipped/duplicate generation, invalid state transition, or witness mismatch exits 2. Git may establish repository provenance, but it is never the predecessor byte store and never substitutes for the in-file chain. - **Threat model (explicit non-goal):** this detects honest-agent error — an accidental hand-edit, a buggy script, or a third party without repository commit access — not a hostile actor who already holds legitimate commit/push authority on this same repository or account. No purely file-based provenance check can defend against a fully privileged insider rewriting history, and this contract does not claim to. - **Concurrency (I19):** `bootstrapBaseline`/`advanceBaseline`'s write-temp-then-rename gives single-write atomicity and crash-safety only; it assumes a single-process, serialized caller and does not by itself arbitrate two genuinely concurrent invocations racing to read-modify-write this file. - **Transition witness (D14):** Both variants require exact `transition_witness`. `bootstrapBaseline` binds canonical C14 input with null predecessor; `advanceBaseline` binds canonical C12 input and the exact immediately preceding in-envelope record bytes. `loadBaselineAuthority` replays the whole envelope and refuses any record not reachable through those named transitions. - **Compatibility:** Additive fields forbidden until schema version bump.

design_records.title: CanonicalSemanticModelIR
design_records.text: - **Owner:** R3-01 - **Consumers:** R1-02, R5-01 - **Shape/behavior:** Projected semantic_model object keys exactly version string "2", criteria, anchors, design_records, verification_definitions. criteria items keys exactly id, text, kind, owner. anchors items keys exactly id, type, target, role, access, action. design_records items keys exactly id, kind, title, text. verification_definitions items keys exactly id, subject_criteria, subject_owner, proof_criteria, proof_owner, evidence_anchor, decision_refs, method, expected, negative, reachability; **method is a tagged union on `kind`**: variant `command` has keys exactly `kind`, `value` (`kind` fixed `"command"`); variant `inspection` has keys exactly `kind`, `target`, `anchor_ref` (`kind` fixed `"inspection"`); no third shape is valid. reachability keys exactly entrypoint, anchor_refs. Normalize: LF line endings for multi-line text fields; collapse internal whitespace runs to single space for criterion and record text titles only when producing compare bytes; unique IDs; **all top-level arrays (criteria, anchors, design_records, verification_definitions) and all nested set arrays (subject_criteria, proof_criteria, decision_refs, reachability.anchor_refs, after de-duplication) sort using one exact ASCII ordinal string comparator**: for strings a, b compare UTF-16 code unit by code unit and return -1/0/1 on the first difference (equivalent to `a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0` in JavaScript) — this is not `localeCompare`, ICU collation, or an implementer-chosen "natural sort"; IDs and set values in this contract are restricted to ASCII, so the ordinal comparator is deterministic across hosts and Node builds; object keys via stable JSON key sort. Equality is byte equality of stable normalized JSON. semanticDigest is sha256 of those canonical bytes formatted sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex. Disagreement report JSON keys exactly: paths array of JSON Pointer strings, leftValueDigest sha256 colon plus 64 hex, rightValueDigest sha256 colon plus 64 hex, legacyDigest, irDigest, mode, run_id string, timestamp ISO string; must not contain private fixture bodies. Mode authority: off no compare; shadow markdown authority report-only on disagreement; promote IR authority hard-fail readiness on disagreement; rollback returns to shadow or off deterministically by writer task. - **Compatibility:** Matches schema 2.1 MODEL_FIELDS and item fields in spec-semantic-model.cjs, including the existing command/inspection method tagged union. R3-01 replaces existing `localeCompare`-based sort call sites in spec-semantic-model.cjs with the ASCII ordinal comparator above and proves cross-host sort parity in owned tests.

design_records.title: ReleaseReceipt
design_records.text: - **Owner:** R5-01 - **Consumers:** R0-01 - **Shape/behavior:** JSON object with keys exactly: schema_version fixed string "1"; receipt_id non-empty string; status fixed string "published"; baselineAuthorityDigest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex equal to the current C10 authority record digest; baselineGeneration non-negative integer equal to the current authority generation; freezeDigest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex over the current C9 FreezeManifest bytes; candidateDigest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex equal to the current freeze candidateDigest; treeDigest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex equal to the current freeze treeDigest; packageVersion non-empty string equal to the current freeze packageVersion; releaseCommit a valid full git object id that is a descendant of or equal to the current authority baselineCommit; artifactPath a repo-relative path restricted to `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/` naming a real npm `.tgz` file; artifactDigest sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex over the packaged release artifact bytes; resolvedFailureIds sorted-unique array of C15 `failure_id` strings that must be the **exact sorted-set equal** of the current freeze's own `remediatedFailureIds` (C9, I12) — never independently chosen, supplemented, or trimmed at receipt-authoring time; empty exactly when the freeze's `remediatedFailureIds` is empty. releaseReceiptDigest is computed externally as sha256 of the canonical stable-JSON receipt bytes; it is never a field inside the receipt itself, so no circular digest is possible. Once validated, `advanceBaseline` durably persists these exact receipt bytes at the canonical path `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/release-receipt.json` (gitignored/mutable, same directory as the freeze state) as event (A) — strictly before it rotates the authority record (event B, I11) — and its own idempotency check independently re-verifies, and idempotently repairs when necessary, this same canonical evidence rather than trusting a digest match alone. This is the sole source `resolveFailure` independently re-reads to verify what was actually published (I13), never a caller-supplied digest or claim. - **advanceBaseline: exact validate-before-mutate order, idempotent resume with evidence repair, no faked cross-file atomicity (I11).** Publishing a release is exactly three independent single-file-atomic persistence events — **(A)** persist the canonical C12 receipt bytes, **(B)** rotate the C10 authority record (the sole publication checkpoint), **(C)** append a C15 `resolved` event per id — never a cross-file transaction, and this contract does not pretend otherwise. `advanceBaseline` owns (A) and (B) as two sequential sub-steps of one invocation; `resolveFailure` (C15) owns (C), invoked separately by R5-01's orchestration strictly after `advanceBaseline` returns success. `advanceBaseline`'s exact sequence, always in this order and never reordered or parallelized: - **(1) Idempotency check, before any other read or write:** compute `releaseReceiptDigest` over the supplied receipt bytes. If it already equals the *current* C10 authority's own published `releaseReceiptDigest` **and** authority `state = released`, this exact release was already published — by this call or a prior one — and `advanceBaseline` does **not** blindly return success on the digest match alone. Instead: **(1a)** read the canonical persisted receipt at `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/release-receipt.json` (resolved from a fixed trusted root — no per-call caller path); if it exists, conforms to the exact C12 schema, and its own recomputed digest equals the authority's published digest, the evidence is intact — return success immediately without touching the freeze, candidate, or ledger, and without re-validating anything else (the ordinary idempotent-resume case, e.g. after a crash following a prior successful (B)). **(1b)** If that canonical file is missing, unreadable, or fails schema/digest verification, but the *supplied* receipt bytes for this call independently conform to the exact C12 schema and their own recomputed digest equals the authority's published digest, those supplied bytes are the same cryptographically-proven-correct evidence, merely lost from disk: repair (A) idempotently by writing those exact bytes to the canonical path (write-temp-then-rename), re-read and re-verify the write (schema + digest), then return success — this is **recovery of evidence for an already-published fact, not a new publication**, and requires no re-validation of the freeze, candidate, or any other current-state field. **(1c)** If the supplied bytes themselves fail schema validation, or their own recomputed digest does not equal the authority's published digest, exit 2 without writing — never reconstruct or guess receipt content from an unverified source. - **(2) Otherwise** (the supplied receipt's digest does not match the current published digest — a genuinely new release candidate), `advanceBaseline` performs every read-only validation — baselineAuthorityDigest/baselineGeneration equal the current authority, freezeDigest equals the current on-disk freeze bytes, candidateDigest/treeDigest/packageVersion equal the current freeze, `resolvedFailureIds` is the exact sorted-set equal of the current freeze's `remediatedFailureIds` (I12; any divergence exits 2 without writing — this is what makes it impossible for a receipt to claim resolution of an id that was never actually proven-remediated at gate/freeze time), releaseCommit exists and is reachable from the current baseline, status is exactly "published", **and independently re-hashes the actual bytes at `artifactPath` to confirm they equal `artifactDigest`** — rejecting a symlinked, missing, or content-mismatched `artifactPath` with exit 2 before any write; the artifact is never trusted from the receipt's own claim alone; any mismatch exits 2 without writing anything. - **Event (A):** only after every check in (2) passes, `advanceBaseline` durably persists the exact validated receipt bytes at the canonical path `packages/spec/.cafekit-release/release-receipt.json` (write-temp-then-rename, its own atomic op) — strictly **before** any authority mutation. **Read-after-write verification, symmetric with (1b) (closes the gap where a first publish trusted its own write call blindly):** immediately after this write, `advanceBaseline` re-reads the canonical file it just produced and verifies it — an exact byte match, or equivalently a freshly recomputed digest plus exact C12 schema match — against the receipt bytes it just supplied, exactly the same verification (1b)'s repair path already performs on its own write. A mismatch (a physically corrupted write, a concurrent clobber, or a filesystem fault) throws fail-closed immediately, strictly before (B) ever runs — the C10 authority is left exactly as it was, never rotated, and `advanceBaseline` never returns `published`. **Observable residual on a crash between (A) and (B):** the canonical receipt file exists and is valid, but the C10 authority record and the C15 ledger are both unchanged — a staged, not-yet-published receipt, never described as "nothing written." A retry re-enters at (1)/(2): the idempotency check at (1) will not yet match (authority is still unrotated), so retry proceeds through (2) and (A) again — (A) is naturally idempotent (identical bytes replace identical bytes) — then (B). - **Event (B):** only after (A) has completed, `advanceBaseline` performs its one atomic authority write and the sole "this release is published" checkpoint: the new released C10 authority stores this externally computed `releaseReceiptDigest` and `previousBaselineDigest` per C10's provenance rule, sets `generation = priorGeneration + 1`, sets `baselineCommit = releaseCommit`, and invalidates the current freeze — written via a single-file atomic replace (write-temp-then-rename). `advanceBaseline` itself never calls `resolveFailure` and never touches the ledger. - **Event (C):** separately, and strictly *after* `advanceBaseline` has returned success (whether freshly published in this call, idempotently confirmed via (1a), or idempotently repaired via (1b)), the release orchestration (R5-01, `benchmark-workflow.mjs`) invokes `resolveFailure` once per id in `resolvedFailureIds` — a set already verified (in (2), or already proven correct at original publish time on the idempotent path) to exactly equal the freeze's gate-proven `remediatedFailureIds` (I12) — in any order among ids. `resolveFailure` never trusts that it is being called at the right time, and never trusts a caller-supplied digest or id claim (I13): it independently re-loads the *current* C10 authority, independently re-reads the exact receipt bytes from the canonical `release-receipt.json` (guaranteed present by (A)'s completion, including via the (1b) repair path), recomputes `releaseReceiptDigest` over those bytes, and refuses (exit 2, no write) unless `state = released`, the recomputed digest exactly equals the authority's own published `releaseReceiptDigest`, the receipt bytes conform to the exact C12 schema, and the `failure_id` it is asked to append is itself a member of that receipt's own `resolvedFailureIds` array — so neither a caller-side ordering bug that invoked `resolveFailure` before (B) ever committed this receipt, nor a caller citing an unrelated open failure alongside a correct digest, can ever record a spurious `resolved` event. `resolveFailure` is independently idempotent per id (see C15). - **Crash/resume semantics, exact (three events, not two):** a crash before (A) leaves nothing written — retry re-enters at (1)/(2). A crash after (A) but before (B) leaves the staged, valid, unpublished receipt described above — retry re-enters at (1)/(2)/(A), idempotent, then (B). A crash after (B) but before any (C) call leaves C10 already rotated (and the freeze already, correctly, invalid) — resuming is re-invoking `advanceBaseline` again (the hardened idempotency check at (1), which verifies or repairs the canonical receipt rather than blindly trusting the digest match) followed by re-running the `resolveFailure` loop, which independently skips any id already resolved with a matching digest and completes the rest; a crash mid-(C)-loop across multiple ids resumes the same way, per id. A crash, disk fault, or tamper that destroys or corrupts the canonical receipt file *after* (B) has already published is recovered by the (1b) repair path on the next `advanceBaseline` retry, using the same supplied receipt bytes that originally justified the publish — never a re-derivation from freeze/candidate state and never treated as a new publication. No separate reconciliation command exists or is needed — resume is always "call the same two functions again with the same receipt." **Concurrency (I19):** every step above assumes a single-process, serialized caller for a given release; the write-temp-then-rename atomicity of (A)/(B)/(C) guarantees crash-safe resume, not arbitration between two genuinely concurrent `advanceBaseline`/`resolveFailure` invocations — that is out of scope, and this contract does not claim otherwise. - **Compatibility:** Additive fields forbidden until schema version bump.

design_records.title: SemanticReviewHistory
design_records.text: - **Owner:** R1-01 - **Consumers:** R1-02, R5-01 - **Shape/behavior:** `spec.json.validation.semantic_review_history` object with keys exactly `lineage_id`, `entries`. `lineage_id` is sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex over a stable-JSON object over the immutable top-level spec.json fields `feature_name` and `created_at`; scaffold and finalizer derive it, callers never set it directly. `entries` is an append-only array; each entry has keys exactly `sequence`, `semantic_digest`, `review_receipt_digest`, `verdict`, `lifecycle_disposition`, `blocking_count`, `attempt_index`, `review_epoch`. `sequence` starts at 0 and increases by exactly 1 per real append. `semantic_digest` and `review_receipt_digest` are sha256 colon plus 64 lowercase hex; `review_receipt_digest` hashes the full completed C2 receipt bytes so history never duplicates findings, unresolved_decisions, or counterexamples — only the digest and the minimal derivation fields below are stored. `verdict` is PASS or FAIL; `lifecycle_disposition` is CONTINUE or BLOCKED; `blocking_count` is a non-negative integer equal to the count of blocking findings plus blocking unresolved_decisions on the receipt that produced this entry. `review_epoch` is a non-negative integer equal to the count of prior entries in the same `lineage_id` whose `verdict` is `PASS` (epoch 0 before any PASS; a `PASS` entry is stamped with the epoch it closes, and the next entry after it opens `review_epoch + 1`). `attempt_index` is 0..2 and equals the count of prior entries in the **same `review_epoch`** whose `verdict` is FAIL — not the whole lineage's FAIL count (see I10) — with 0, 1, 2 naming the first, second, and third attempt of that epoch respectively; FAIL at 2 sets `lifecycle_disposition BLOCKED` and blocks a fourth attempt of that epoch from ever occurring (index 3 never appears within it, and a `BLOCKED` epoch is never reopened — see I10). The current completed C2 receipt is appended atomically with the readiness decision it produced; a receipt whose `review_receipt_digest` equals **any existing entry's digest anywhere in the same lineage — not only the latest entry** — is a replay and is not appended again and does not increment `attempt_index` or `review_epoch` (idempotent, deduped against the full lineage; this whole-lineage dedupe rule is unchanged by epoch scoping). **Reject-before-append check (exact mechanism, closes the "does the fourth attempt actually get refused" gap):** before computing `attempt_index`/`review_epoch` for a new entry or appending it, the finalizer first inspects the latest entry already recorded for the current `review_epoch` in this lineage (if any). If that latest entry already carries `lifecycle_disposition = BLOCKED`, the finalizer refuses the entire operation outright — it does not compute an `attempt_index` for what would be a fourth attempt, does not append any entry, and does not set `ready_for_implementation`; it exits with an explicit epoch-blocked refusal before any other C2/C13 processing runs. This check is unconditional and runs before dedupe/idempotency handling, so a replay of an already-`BLOCKED` epoch's own digest is still recognized as the idempotent no-op it already was (whole-lineage dedupe above), while any genuinely new, non-replay receipt arriving against a `BLOCKED` epoch is refused outright rather than silently computing an out-of-range `attempt_index`. `lineage_id` is stable across ordinary semantic authoring edits — it changes only when the spec itself is recreated (a new `created_at`), never as a side effect of editing requirements.md/design.md/tasks (see I6).
